ideas.pitch: A high-performance autonomous micromouse featuring real-time Flood Fill maze mapping optimized for high-speed diagonal cutting.
ideas.problem_statement: Micromouse Challenge — Navigate the Maze, Beat the Clock: Build an autonomous robot that can map and solve a 10×10 grid maze on its own.
ideas.title: FloodFill-X: Adaptive Speed-Run Micromouse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the winning hardware and robotics pattern by focusing on low-level firmware optimization (Flood Fill algorithm in C++) and reliable dead reckoning within tight physical constraints.

ideas.pitch: A robust Micromouse utilizing sensor fusion between ToF distance sensors and a 6-DoF IMU to prevent wall collisions and dead-reckon through the 10x10 maze.
ideas.problem_statement: Micromouse Challenge — Navigate the Maze, Beat the Clock: Build an autonomous robot that can map and solve a 10×10 grid maze on its own.
ideas.title: IMU-Fusion Wall-Hugger Bot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses the strict wall-collision penalty rule directly by combining infrared distance sensors with inertial measurement unit tracking for ultra-precise turns.

ideas.pitch: A compact autonomous mouse equipped with an optical flow sensor to eliminate wheel slip and achieve maximum velocity on the speed run.
ideas.problem_statement: Micromouse Challenge — Navigate the Maze, Beat the Clock: Build an autonomous robot that can map and solve a 10×10 grid maze on its own.
ideas.title: MicroVision: On-Board Edge Optical Flow Micromouse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages advanced sensor hardware that stands out among standard encoders, providing precise displacement tracking within the 19x19 cm bounding box.

ideas.pitch: A custom dual-layer PCB design acting as both the structural chassis and the circuit board to maintain the strict under-90mm height limit.
ideas.problem_statement: Micromouse Challenge — Navigate the Maze, Beat the Clock: Build an autonomous robot that can map and solve a 10×10 grid maze on its own.
ideas.title: CompactCell: Modular PCB-Chassis Micromouse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Showcases custom hardware fabrication and clean engineering design, directly matching the winning custom electronics pattern.

ideas.pitch: A micromouse that stores solved maze geometries in non-volatile memory, allowing instant optimal speed runs across consecutive trials.
ideas.problem_statement: Micromouse Challenge — Navigate the Maze, Beat the Clock: Build an autonomous robot that can map and solve a 10×10 grid maze on its own.

ideas.why_it_could_win: Maximizes points by optimizing the multiple-run format required by the competition rules, jumping straight from search mode to record-breaking speed runs.
